title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and thoroughly cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, the pregnant woman's body needs to be provided with adequate nutrients to support the development of the fetus. One of the most important nutrients is folic acid, which helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. Additionally, iron and other nutrients also play a crucial role in fetal development.

## Folic Acid and Iron: Two Essential Nutrients

Folic acid is a crucial nutrient that helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should take 400 micrograms of folic acid daily. Iron is also an essential nutrient that supports fetal development and prevents anemia in the pregnant woman.

## Safe Foods and Cooking Methods

During the first trimester, pregnant women should prioritize safe foods and cooking methods. Foods like meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products should be cooked thoroughly to avoid the risk of food poisoning. Additionally, pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi, sashimi, and other raw or undercooked foods.

## Ensuring Adequate Hydration and Nutrition

To ensure adequate hydration and nutrition, pregnant women should drink at least 8 glasses of water per day and eat balanced meals. Meals should include nutrient-rich foods like meat, fish, eggs, dairy products, fruits, and vegetables.

## Practical Tips for First Trimester Nutrition

Here are some practical tips for first trimester nutrition:

* Eat balanced and varied meals
* Drink plenty of water each day
* Avoid raw or undercooked foods
* Take folic acid and iron supplements daily
* Consult a [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/topics/pregnancy-meal-planner) for a personalized nutrition plan

## When to Seek Help

If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about first trimester nutrition, they should seek help from their healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. Additionally, they can consult reputable sources like [our website](/blog) for accurate and helpful information.
